- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent peak for next 7–14 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending up, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for next 3–7 days.
- Model frequently underestimates in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed; apply 1–2% upward bias for first 5–10 days.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model lags; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For sentiment-heavy periods (e.g., 3+ consecutive 1.00), model overfits; apply 2–5% downward correction for next 7–14 days.
